title: Indian All-Rounder Mahipal Lomror Signs Six-Match Deal With Surrey for County Championship
excerpt: The 26-year-old left-hander from Rajasthan joins a growing Indian contingent in English county cricket, bolstering Surrey's title push for the final stretch of the season.
body:
• Mahipal Lomror has signed a six-match deal with Surrey to play the final six County Championship matches of the 2026 season.
  • The Indian all-rounder brings strong first-class credentials — 2,481 runs at 38.16 and 47 wickets across 42 matches — to the reigning county champions.
  • Lomror joins compatriot Rahul Chahar at The Oval, making Surrey one of two counties fielding multiple Indian overseas players this season.
  • The signing continues a growing trend of uncapped Indian cricketers testing themselves in English conditions outside the IPL window.

Surrey Bolster Squad With Indian All-Rounder

Surrey have signed Indian all-rounder Mahipal Lomror on a short-term deal for the remaining six matches of the 2026 County Championship season, the club confirmed on August 14. The left-handed batter and slow left-arm orthodox spinner will provide both middle-order depth and a spin option as the defending champions chase another Division One title.

Lomror, 26, arrives at The Oval with significant domestic experience. In 42 first-class matches for Rajasthan, he has scored 2,481 runs at an average of 38.16, including five centuries and 15 half-centuries. His highest score of 133 came in a Ranji Trophy fixture, and he famously hit a triple century against Uttarakhand in November 2024 that underscored his ability to bat long in red-ball cricket.

"For any cricketer, the County Championship is a huge opportunity."

— Mahipal Lomror, on his Surrey call-up

A Growing Indian Presence in County Cricket

Lomror is not the only Indian plying his trade at The Oval this season. Leg-spinner Rahul Chahar, who took a record-breaking 10-for on his Surrey debut in 2025, returned for the final eight Championship matches. The pair will overlap for at least six fixtures, giving Surrey a rare twin Indian overseas presence.

The 2026 County Championship season has seen a notable influx of Indian talent across England. Yuzvendra Chahal is playing for Northamptonshire in the second half of the campaign, R Sai Kishore signed a six-match deal with Gloucestershire after impressing at Surrey last year, and Jaydev Unadkat is turning out for Sussex. None of these players have been regulars in India's international squads, but county cricket offers red-ball exposure and conditions that Indian domestic pitches rarely replicate.

What Lomror Brings to Surrey

Known primarily as an aggressive middle-order batter, Lomror made his name in the IPL with Royal Challengers Bengaluru before joining Gujarat Titans and later Mumbai Indians as a replacement player. His left-arm spin, while not his primary skill, adds tactical flexibility — he has claimed 47 first-class wickets at 34.12, including one five-wicket haul.

Surrey will be hoping Lomror can translate his domestic run-scoring form to English conditions. His record in multi-day cricket suggests a player comfortable batting time, a quality that county cricket rewards. His left-arm spin could also prove useful on wearing pitches in the back end of the English season, when surfaces tend to offer more turn.

What It Means for the Championship Race

Surrey, under Gareth Batty, have been dominant in English domestic cricket in recent years. Adding Lomror to a squad already featuring Chahar signals their intent to leave nothing to chance in the final push. With Sean Abbott having completed his eight-match stint at the start of the season, Lomror effectively slots in as the Australian departing opens an overseas registration spot.

The first Test between England and Pakistan begins at Headingley on August 19, meaning several Surrey players — most notably Dan Lawrence, who was recalled to the England squad — could be absent during parts of Lomror's stint, making his availability even more valuable.

Looking Ahead

For Lomror, the Surrey spell offers a chance to build a case for higher honours. Several Indian cricketers have used successful county stints as springboards to international recognition, and a productive run in Division One would bolster his credentials ahead of the next Ranji Trophy season and the IPL mega auction cycle. His six-match window begins with Surrey's next Championship fixture in late August.
